claim: NullPropagatedOperands recurses into Left/Right for every SqlBinaryExpression operator, including AndAlso/OrElse which do not propagate NULL under three-valued logic; operands inside boolean expressions are marked null-propagated, DropNotNullChecks removes their IS NOT NULL guard, and CASE WHEN x IS NOT NULL THEN <bool expr> ELSE NULL END collapses to the bare boolean, returning true/false where null is required (e.g. x.NullableIntA != null ? (bool?)(x.NullableIntA == x.NullableIntB) : null returns False for A=null,B=null). Executed before/after comparison shows six regressing shapes; the new tests only project int?/string results so miss the bool? case; fix is an operator allow-list.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` treats `AND`/`OR` as null-propagating, so the guard is dropped from `CASE WHEN x IS NOT NULL THEN <boolean expr over x> ELSE NULL END` and the query returns `true`/`false` where it must return `null`

claim: The same SqlBinaryExpression arm also treats ExpressionType.Coalesce as null-propagating; COALESCE(a, b) does not propagate null from a, so dropping a IS NOT NULL from CASE WHEN a IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(a, b) ELSE NULL END yields b instead of NULL. Not reachable via the stock pipeline today (?? becomes a SqlFunctionExpression; QuerySqlGenerator.GetOperator throws for binary Coalesce), but the operator is legal per IsValidOperator and buildable via public MakeBinary; excluded by the same allow-list.
raw: #2 🟡 Medium: `Coalesce` is also traversed as null-propagating
